To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the calcium-conduction activity of the translocating CyaA conformer controls the path and speed of endocytic membrane removal of bystander pore-forming conformers and that the resulting positive feedback loop of enhanced cell permeabilization is the main determinant of CyaA-mediated phagocyte killing.

the calcium-conductive translocating conformers of CyaA control the path and kinetics endocytic removal from the cell membrane of the bystander toxin pores and this triggers a positive feedback cycle of exacerbated cell permeability.
the calcium-conductive activity of the translocating CyaA conformer controls the path and rate of toxin pore removal from phagocyte cytoplasmic membranes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel role of calcium influx in regulating the endocytic fate of CyaA and its hemolysin activity.
the mechanism of toxin-induced permeabilization of phagocyte membrane, and the role of calcium influx in this process.
the role of calcium-conducting conformer of CytA as a molecular switch that determines the fate of the pore-forming toxin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

calcium influx rescues the translocating CyaA conformer from the rapid endocytic removal from phagocyte cell membrane and this enables CyaA pores to permeabilize the cytoplasmatic membrane of phagocytic cells.
CyaA is an example of a protein that can use its own enzymatic activity (calcium influx) to regulate the activity of its other domain (hemolytic pore formation).
calcium-conducting translocating conformers of CyaA are essential to enable cell permeabilization by bystander CyaA pores.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the calcium-conductive activity of Cya toxin is essential for its ability to kill phagocytes.

the calcium-conduction activity of Cya toxin enables the toxin to control the path of its removal from phagocyte cell surface, and this is essential for the toxin to exert its multiple pathophysiological activities.
the translocating and pore-forming conformers of CyaA are two sides of the same coin, where the calcium-conductance of the former is a prerequisite for the cell-permeabilizing activity of the latter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the calcium-conductive activity of the translocating CyaA conformer is essential for its ability to trigger phagocyte lysis.
CyaA employs a novel mechanism to regulate the path of endocytosed toxin pores and the fate of phagocytes.
